result.title: Do Occupancy World Models Really Follow Actions?
result.summary: Occupancy world models predict future 3D scenes conditioned on ego actions, yet their predictions may not faithfully follow the specified trajectory under counterfactual actions. Because driving datasets provide sparse coverage of alternative trajectories for each scene, existing models learn the spatial effect of ego motion implicitly from observed scene--trajectory combinations, which may entangle action effects with scene--trajectory correlations. We propose ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer that grounds future prediction in action-induced geometric correspondence across ego-centric frames. ReCast decouples historical encoding from future decoding and aligns deformable interactions using relative ego transformations, while retaining flexibility for non-rigid scene evolution. We also introduce a counterfactual action-faithfulness benchmark covering in-distribution, tail, and out-of-distribution trajectories. On Occ3D-nuScenes, ReCast achieves competitive standard forecasting performance while improving counterfactual forecasting, with particularly clear gains under out-of-distribution trajectories.

AI.brief_summary: 该文质疑占用式世界模型是否真正按给定自车轨迹预测未来 3D 场景，提出 ReCast：解耦历史编码与未来解码，用相对自车位姿对齐可变形交互，并构建反事实动作忠实性基准（含分布内、尾部和分布外轨迹）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其反事实动作忠实性评测可用于核查 latent 状态是否真正依赖条件输入而非场景—轨迹相关性，几何对应式状态更新也可能为视觉证据筛选与状态更新的设计提供线索，但属驾驶世界模型，与 VLM 推理的迁移需自行核查。
